newsitem.title: UK: London stocks hit record, Nikkei posts gains.
newsitem.headline: London stocks hit record, Nikkei posts gains.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Wednesday.

LONDON - The FTSE 100 sailed through the 4,000 mark with ease to close at a record for the second day running as a strong international bond market and Wall Street strength pushed blue chip prices higher. The FTSE 100 ended at 4,015.1, up 22.9 points.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse trade sharply higher, buoyed by overnight Wall Street gains and a higher dollar. The 30-share DAX index ended up 20.77 points to 2,676.50. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 2,685.29.
PARIS - French shares closed higher in robust volume, bolstered by firm bonds, strength on Wall Street and buying by U.S. investors. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 18.63 points at 2,141.84.

ZURICH - Swiss shares lost steam towards the end of the session as profit taking set in after the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) failed to overcome a resistance level around 3,765/70 points. The Broad SPI ended up 0.52 percent, or 12.40 points, at 2,407.16.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended marginally firmer after wandering narrowly in both positive and negative territory for most of the day. The 225-issue Nikkei average closed 35.63 points or 0.17 percent higher at 21,498.60.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks snared another 1996 closing high, despite some profit-taking after recent gains, as investors remained bullish on the outlook of the market. The Hang Seng index closed 30.66 points higher at 11,951.88, the highest close since Feb. 4, 1994.

SYDNEY - Australian shares stormed to their highest close in five months as a flood of afternoon buying interest inspired by surging share price index futures, pushed turnover above the A$1 billion mark ($795 million). By the close the All Ordinaries index jumped 29.1 points to 2,314.6.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares jumped, boosted by powerful bull markets all around the globe and a stronger rand. Dealers said strong gains on Wall Street and Britain's FTSE-100 index had provided the impetus behind the rise. A stronger rand and a recovering bullion price had been the icing on the cake to a good day's business, they added. The overall share index ended at 6,997.1, up 100.9 points in strong volumes, while industrials jumped to 8,204.2, up 70.1 points. A bullion price struggling bravely to breach the $380 an ounce barrier also boosted golds and meant that the gold index posted the biggest gain of the day, up 3.26 percent or 54.6 points to 1,731.8.
